absent: No probing, caching, locking, or concurrency rules appear in these fragments.
No accessors, entry points, exported functions, or runtime services appear beyond record layouts and subleaf bounds.
No state machines, initialization sequences, or error handling appear.
No semantic definitions of enumerated code values such as domain types, cache types, or target types appear beyond their labels.

findings.text: Time calibration record exposes three unsigned quantities plus one reserved word: ratio denominator, ratio numerator, and nominal crystal frequency in hertz. A consumer combines ratio with nominal value to derive timer frequency.
Frequency record reports base, maximum, and bus reference frequencies in megahertz, each occupying the low half of successive words with high bits reserved, and the final word fully reserved.

System-on-chip identification uses a base record for maximum subleaf index, vendor code with industry-scheme flag, project identifier, and stepping identifier. Each continuation record carries sixteen bytes of vendor brand text spread evenly across four words.
Continuation indices for the SoC brand string run from one through three inclusive.

Translation-cache descriptor reports enumeration bound, supported page sizes, sharing among logical processors, associativity width, set count, cache category and level, fully associative indication, and addressable identifier limit. Remaining bit ranges are reserved.
Translation-cache enumeration accepts subleaf indices zero through thirty one inclusive.

Key locker record groups usage restrictions, instruction and state support, and key-loading controls across three words with the final word reserved. It distinguishes privilege-only use, encrypt versus decrypt denial, narrow versus wide handling, supervisor backup support, and initialization-key options.
Hybrid core identification places native model number and core category together in the first word and reserves the remaining three words, letting software distinguish core types in one package.
Platform configuration enumeration record carries a type discriminator plus three target identifiers. Repeating the leaf with successive subleaves enumerates the supported targets.
Platform configuration enumeration accepts subleaf indices zero through thirty one inclusive.

Branch-record capability record describes stack depth mask, clearing across deep sleep, address flavor, privilege and branch filtering with call-stack mode, and extended logging for mispredict indication, timing, branch typing, and event bitmap width.

Matrix extension description uses a base word advertising the highest palette or subleaf index. The palette record reports total and per-tile byte sizes, row width, tile count, and maximum rows per tile, with remaining space reserved.
Matrix multiply geometry record reserves three words and reports in one word the maximum height dimension and maximum vector width dimension, with the rest of that word reserved.

Extended topology record reports shift width for the current level, logical processor count for the domain, domain level and type codes, and current x2APIC identifier. Iterating subleaves walks from narrower toward wider domains.
Extended topology enumeration accepts subleaf indices zero through five inclusive.
History-reset record reports the count of valid subleaves as maximum index plus one in the first word, a thread-director reset capability in the second word, and reserves everything else.

Trust-domain vendor record reserves the first word and carries twelve bytes of vendor text across the remaining words in shuffled register order, so the later words are transposed relative to linear byte order.

Performance monitoring root advertises which follow-on subleaves exist plus selected control abilities, followed by bitmap words for general and fixed counters and by auto-reload source and trigger sets for both counter classes.

Performance monitoring tail covers supported architectural events, precise-event record group encodings with an allow-in-record control, and precise-event distribution bitmaps for general and fixed counters.
Hypervisor identification record reports the maximum hypervisor leaf index plus twelve bytes of provider text in linear register order across the remaining words.

Synthetic kernel feature pages pack operating-system level capabilities and mitigation selections into dense single-bit flags across two pages. The first page covers timer behavior, topology, power and performance interfaces, cache and memory allocation technologies, virtualization assists, paravirtual interfaces, confidential-computing roles, and speculation controls. The second page covers machine-check recovery, branch-history clearing, performance-control variants, and return-prediction handling.

Synthetic bug page packs historical functional defects and transient-execution vulnerability indicators into dense single-bit flags across two words, with remaining words reserved. It separates legacy errata from side-channel exposures affecting isolation, sampling, branch prediction, and microcode currency.

Extended-range root reports the maximum extended index plus twelve bytes of processor vendor text across the remaining words in shuffled register order, with later words transposed relative to linear byte order.

Each record is a 128-bit image of four output words in architectural order, built from unsigned bitfields whose widths sum to thirty two per word. Reserved ranges are padding without meaning and consumers ignore them.
Enumerable leaves advertise their own bound in the base record as a maximum subleaf index or subleaf count, so software iterates only defined indices without probing undefined values.

Some vendor text leaves do not follow linear word order: the bytes that belong in the middle of the string sit in the last word and vice versa, so naive concatenation in register order corrupts the string. Consumers must reorder by documented byte ranges.
